commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(bus): make heartbeat refresh opt-in so on-behalf events cannot spoof liveness (#930)
commits.body:
logEvent() refreshed the target agent's last_heartbeat as an unconditional
side-effect of every event write. When the daemon logs an event on another
agent's behalf — delivering an inbound Telegram via recordInboundTelegram ->
logEvent('telegram_received') — it refreshed that agent's heartbeat even if the
agent's session was wedged, spoofing liveness. A stale-heartbeat detector reading
this signal therefore fails open: a wedged agent that keeps receiving messages
never looks stale.

Make the refresh opt-in via a new { refreshHeartbeat?: boolean } param on
logEvent, default OFF (fail-safe). The 7 in-session/agent-own call sites opt in;
the 2 on-behalf writers (recordInboundTelegram delivery, pty runtime-error event)
do not, so a wedged agent's heartbeat can no longer be refreshed by traffic it
did not act on. Default-off means any future daemon-side logEvent site is safe by
construction. Existing tests that asserted the old unconditional refresh are
updated; adds spoof-guard tests for both the default-off path and the
recordInboundTelegram delivery path.

Co-authored-by: Boris <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(daemon): detect silent agent dormancy on `cortextos status` with per-agent cadence threshold (#929)
commits.body:
* fix(daemon): detect silent agent dormancy on `cortextos status`

Adds a pure dormancy detector: an enabled agent whose heartbeat is stale
relative to its own liveness baseline is flagged `dormant` on the status
surface. Two baselines from one predicate: mapped agents use process
uptime (staleness clamped to uptime, so a fleet bounce never flags the
whole fleet); enabled-but-unmapped agents use time since daemon start
(roster-diff). mapped/unmapped never enters the gate, only the reason.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(daemon): derive silent-dormancy threshold from per-agent heartbeat cadence

The dormancy detector defaulted every agent to a 30m expected interval, so a
healthy agent on a multi-hour heartbeat cadence was silently flagged dormant for
most of each cycle. Derive each agent's threshold from its OWN configured
heartbeat cron cadence plus a fixed additive jitter margin instead.

- Replace the x3 staleness multiplier with an additive JITTER_MARGIN_MS (45m):
  jitter is ~constant wall-clock (a beat delayed by a long turn), not
  proportional to cadence, so a multiplier over-inflates slow-cadence thresholds.
- Add a pure parseHeartbeatIntervalMs (Nh/Nm/Nd + every-N-hours cron) and an
  agent-manager reader that resolves each agent's real heartbeat cadence; wire it
  into both computeDormancy call sites.
- Unparseable / no-heartbeat-cron agents fall to a conservative 24h fallback
  (documented as an unvalidated ceiling; a cadence-tightening follow-up will
  measure healthy-max-idle and tighten it).

Detector stays advisory-only (rendered on 'cortextos status'); no remediation
consumes the flag.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(daemon): suppress futile context-handoff when resume baseline exceeds threshold (#937)
commits.body:
Agents with a heavy resume baseline restart at the handoff threshold, come back already at/above it, and re-fire in a loop until the 3-fire circuit breaker pauses them for 30min — each restart accomplishing nothing, since a handoff cannot reduce a baseline it did not create.

Capture a per-session baseline at the first post-grace reading; in Tier 2, when that baseline is already >= the handoff threshold and context has grown less than WORKFILL_MARGIN (10 points) since, suppress the futile handoff and alert the configured orchestrator once instead of thrashing. A session that starts below threshold and grows into it, or starts high and accumulates real work-fill, still hands off normally. Genuine exhaustion stays caught by the ungated hard-overflow path.

Adds unit tests covering: heavy-baseline suppression + single alert, low-baseline grow-into-threshold still hands off, born-high-then-real-work still hands off, and the unanchored legacy path unchanged.

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(daemon): death-confirmed stop closes duplicate-PTY windows (#931)
commits.body:
AgentProcess.stop() could return with the OS child still alive: the
15s Promise.race grace bound resolves on timeout, node-pty kill() is
SIGHUP-only with no SIGKILL escalation, and re-entrant stop() was a
silent no-op. This let two live PTYs coexist under one agent name and
both emit (duplicate sends) across a restart or stop+start cycle.

Two triggers, one root cause (stop reports done without confirming
OS death; guards key on map-entry identity, not process liveness):
- Window 1 (restartAgent/soft-restart): stop() times out with the
  child alive, the map entry is deleted, and the successor-race guard
  finds no rival to compare, so startAgent spawns a second PTY.
- Window 2 (stop-agent + start-agent IPC pair): the racing startAgent
  reads the entry as pid-less (handle nulled synchronously), takes the
  eviction path whose re-entrant stop() was a no-op, and spawns.

Fix, entirely within AgentProcess.stop():
- Death-confirmed stop: capture the child pid before kill(), and after
  the grace race escalate to SIGKILL and bounded-poll liveness until
  the process is confirmed dead before returning. Gated so a child that
  exits within the grace window never sees SIGKILL (no added latency).
- Join-in-flight re-entry: a re-entrant stop() awaits the same
  death-confirmed teardown instead of returning immediately, so the
  eviction path's await blocks the fresh spawn until the predecessor
  is dead. Closes Window 2 without touching the manager guards.

agent-manager.ts and ipc-server.ts are unchanged.

Tests: agent-process.test.ts gains W1 (SIGHUP-immune child is reaped by
SIGKILL before stop resolves), W2 (re-entrant stop joins the same
teardown; one SIGKILL, both resolve together), and a fast-exit
no-false-kill guard; a new agent-manager-dup-pty-window2 test drives
the manager-level stop+start race (control vs fixed contract). The two
agent-process tests are genuine positive controls (fail on unmodified
stop()). One line added to an existing stop-width test whose minimal
PTY mock omitted getPid().

Known residual: SIGKILL reaps the pty session leader, not a detached
grandchild tree (process-group kill deferred as a broader change).
